newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Gov't says Colombia's June CPI rose 1.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Gov't says Colombia's June CPI rose 1.5 pct.

text.p: The head of the National Planning Department said Colombia's consumer price index rose by about 1.5 percent in June, down slightly from a 1.62 percent increase in May.
"For June, the inflation index should be around 1.5 percent," Planning Department chief Cecilia Lopez said.

She did not elaborate on the figure which is to be announced officially by the National Statistics Department Wednesday morning. But 1.5 percent is below some expectations, given last month's relatively steep 2.1 percent increase in the producer price index.
Lopez, who spoke in brief remarks to reporters at the presidential palace, said foodstuffs were responsible for putting the most inflationary pressures on the economy in June.
If the CPI rose 1.5 percent in June it would mean the index increased by 11.44 percent during the first half of the year.
Inflation for all of 1996 was 21.63 percent and the central bank has set an 18 percent target for this year.
